key_insight: SWITi reduces tiling seams by averaging overlapping sliding-window predictions, spreading posterior-sampling discrepancies across positions instead of concentrating them at fixed tile boundaries.
clinical_relevance: For large biomedical images, it can make model outputs more reliable by reducing artifacts that could be mistaken for real structures or boundaries.
method: Use overlapping sliding-window tiles at test time
Average predictions across shifted tile positions to diffuse seam artifacts
For posterior models, avoid extra forward passes beyond standard MMSE-style inference
evidence_signal: Across three fluorescence microscopy datasets in 2D and 3D, the authors report reduced stitching seams plus improved reconstruction fidelity and resolution using pre-trained published models.
watch_item: Because it targets test-time tiling artifacts, performance still depends on the base model and tile setup, and artifact reduction should be validated on each new dataset.
paper_title: SWITi: Quantifying and Reducing Tiling Artifacts with Sliding Window Inner Tiling
